title: header_range.(offset, length) semantics inconsistency: offset stored but always 0 for root
description: parse.rs build_part line 122-125: header_range = (part.offset_header, part.offset_body - part.offset_header). For the root part, offset_header is 0 (the message starts at byte 0), which is correct. But the tuple field is documented as '(offset, length) into caller's &[u8]' (part.rs line 26). This is actually correct and consistent, but the test in parse_tests.rs line 191 accesses msg.part_index.header_range as (hdr_off, hdr_len) without checking that hdr_off correctly indexes the headers — it only checks that the range doesn't extend past raw.len(). The body_range is tested for content, header_range is not. A future maintainer extending header parsing may silently regress without a test that actually reads the header bytes. Not a current bug, but a test coverage gap in a security-adjacent area.
close_reason: Not a bug: header_range correctly starts at 0 for root (that IS byte 0 of the message). Test coverage gap, not a correctness issue. Low value to add a test just to assert offset==0.
